correctness.rationale: The multiplication xy=T_m(x⊙y) is bounded because l²·l²⊂l¹; T_m has the displayed isometric right inverse, operator norm sqrt(m), and exact head-sum-zero kernel. Every l¹ vector factors as a product via its l¹ right-inverse preimage. For a second orthonormal natural basis, all pairwise coefficient products belong to l¹∩ker T_m. The tail rows each have one unit coefficient in distinct columns, leaving m head columns; their unitary matrix Q has Q^tQ diagonal, and after unimodular square-root diagonal removal becomes a real orthogonal matrix. Conversely every O(m) head rotation works. Injective T|l¹ forces any basis change monomial. Checked exact rational Householder head rotations m=2..7 and finite-window rank equations independently. The infinite conclusion follows from the explicit analytic proof, not finite windows.

value.rationale: A concrete negative resolution of an explicit infinite-dimensional density/rigidity problem, with the smallest possible nonzero kernel and exact positive-dimensional natural-basis moduli, supplies a reusable structural boundary and a one-way general injectivity criterion; not merely a renamed example.

final_claim: For each integer m≥2 over R or C, the given infinite Hilbert evolution algebra has onto bounded T_m with kernel dimension m−1 and A_m²=l¹ dense properly in l², while its orthonormal natural bases modulo phase/permutation are exactly O(m)/B_m; injectivity of T restricted to l¹ is a sufficient general rigidity criterion.
limitations: No classification of nonorthonormal bases or all Hilbert evolution algebras.
